description: Forced-liquidation (強制決済) stream captured live from high-leverage crypto venues, one JSON line per WebSocket message, written by scripts/record_liquidations.py. Recorded because the venues differ in whether they publish history at all: Gate.io serves per-event liquidations for a rolling ~90 days and OKX for ~24 hours, but Binance and BitMEX offer no history whatsoever, so for those the record exists only from the moment recording starts. Full route-by-route measurement in docs/DATA_SOURCES/LIQUIDATION_HISTORY_SURVEY.md. Motivation: the owner's katsuo bot read long wicks as the fingerprint of a liquidation cascade running out of fuel; this dataset observes that flow directly instead of through the wick proxy (docs/STRATEGY_IDEAS.md O-3c, O-6).
source: scripts/record_liquidations.py, run as a resident process by deploy/start_all.bat ("liq-recorder"). Public WebSocket streams, no auth, no orders: Binance USD-M !forceOrder@arr, Bybit v5 linear allLiquidation.BTCUSDT, OKX v5 liquidation-orders (instType SWAP), BitMEX liquidation:XBTUSD.
retention: permanent once written; files are per-venue per-UTC-day and are appended to, never rewritten. Shared to git by deploy/share_logs.bat (git add -f, since data/ is otherwise ignored) so the record is not a single copy on the owner's PC.

venue.meaning: which feed the message came from
venue.unit: string, one of the keys in record_liquidations.VENUES
venue.notes: symbol coverage differs by venue as subscribed: binance_um is ALL symbols (!forceOrder@arr), okx is ALL SWAP contracts (instType SWAP -- a 2026-09-08 probe from the owner PC returned ARB-USDT among others, so this is NOT BTC-only), bybit is BTCUSDT only, bitmex is XBTUSD only. Any BTC-only study must filter, and any volume estimate must account for the two all-symbol feeds

recv_us.meaning: when THIS RECORDER received the message
recv_us.notes: NOT the exchange's own timestamp -- that lives inside raw. Keeping both is deliberate: the difference is the observation delay, which any cross-venue timing study needs. The recorder's clock accuracy is the owner PC's NTP sync (procedure P7)

raw.meaning: the venue's message, parsed from JSON and stored verbatim
raw.notes: deliberately NOT normalised into a common schema. The mechanism is not yet understood, so no field is dropped by the writer's interpretation; normalisation is the reader's job. If a message is not valid JSON it is stored as {"_unparsed": "<text>"}

known_defects: control messages are recorded too: welcome banners, subscribe acknowledgements, pongs and (BitMEX) an initial 'partial' snapshot of currently-open liquidation orders, which is usually empty. A reader must filter for the venue's actual liquidation payload rather than counting lines -- in particular a BitMEX 'partial' with an empty data array is not a liquidation.

reconnects can duplicate messages. The writer appends and never dedupes, on purpose (dropping a line is worse than storing it twice); the reader must dedupe, e.g. on the venue's own order/trade id inside raw.

a gap in the file is indistinguishable from a period with no liquidations. The recorder logs connect/disconnect lines to logs/liquidations.out.log -- that log, not the data file, is what says whether the stream was up. Treat coverage as unknown for any window without a corresponding log.

reachability is route-dependent. SETTLED 2026-09-08 from the owner PC (procedure P8 step 1, docs/DATA_SOURCES/LIQUIDATION_FEED_REACHABILITY.md): all four venues connect, and OKX delivered 8 real liquidations in 60 seconds. The development session had seen Binance REST 451, Bybit REST 403 and an OKX WebSocket reset -- those were artefacts of a datacenter route, not properties of the venues. What is still NOT measured is each venue's liquidation RATE (60 seconds says nothing about it) and long-run connection stability; both come from the recorder's own log once it has run a day.

the daily file rolls on the recorder's UTC date, so a message received either side of midnight lands in the file for the day it was RECEIVED, which can differ from the day inside raw for a venue reporting in another convention.
